title: How old is the Eye of Africa? A polyphase history for the igneous Richat Structure, Mauritania. Lithos 482-483, 107698
author: Abdeina, E. H., Jourdan, F., Chazot, G., Bertrand, H. and Le Gall, B.
point: Gabbro sills intruded 230 to 200 Ma (CAMP); 99 Ma carbonatites; alkaline doming about 100 Myr later made the 40 km dome; erosion since
note: Refereed open-access paper; the gabbro age is modelled from data that gave no robust plateau age, so corr 1. Abstract page read.

title: SOLON of Athens (teaching page)
author: Adams, John Paul (California State University, Northridge)
point: Solon was archon at Athens in 594 BCE
note: University teaching page by a classicist compiling ancient sources on Solon; date undated on page.

title: Persistent Holocene Outflow from the Black Sea to the Eastern Mediterranean Contradicts Noah's Flood Hypothesis
author: Aksu, A. E., Hiscott, R. N., Mudie, P. J., Rochon, A., Kaminski, M. A., Abrajano, T., Yasar, D.
point: Gradual reconnection; 10-11 kyr of low Marmara surface salinity; Bosporus-exit delta active 10 to 9 ka; 7500 line-km seismic, 65 cores, 43 dates
note: Refereed GSA Today science article; abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Persistent Holocene outflow from the Black Sea to the eastern Mediterranean Sea still contradicts the Noah's Flood Hypothesis: A review of 1997-2021 evidence and a regional paleoceanographic synthesis for the latest Pleistocene-Holocene
author: Aksu, A. E., Hiscott, R. N.
point: The gradual-reconnection position restated in 2022
note: Refereed Earth-Science Reviews review; only the abstract opening and archive summary were reachable.

title: Land bridges and rafting theories to explain terrestrial-vertebrate biodiversity on Madagascar. Annual Review of Marine Science 16. doi:10.1146/annurev-marine-032223-025654
author: Ali, J. R.; Hedges, S. B.
point: Madagascar has been an island since 85 Mya, 430 km from Africa; 26 of 30 land-vertebrate lineages arrived by overwater dispersal between 69 and 0 Mya; two are Gondwanan relicts
note: Refereed review of the geological and phylogenetic record. Abstract read via OpenAlex; full text blocked by the publisher's bot check.

title: Mammalian biodiversity on Madagascar controlled by ocean currents. Nature 463: 653-656. doi:10.1038/nature08706
author: Ali, J. R.; Huber, M.
point: Palaeogene surface currents flowed east from Mozambique and Tanzania toward Madagascar, making rafting possible; evidence is inconsistent with a land bridge
note: Refereed modelling study; abstract and editor's summary read on nature.com. Corroboration 1: a single modelling study, since supported by Ali and Hedges 2024.

title: Late Cretaceous bioconnections between Indo-Madagascar and Antarctica: refutation of the Gunnerus Ridge causeway hypothesis. Journal of Biogeography 38: 1855-1872. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2699.2011.02546.x
author: Ali, J. R.; Krause, D. W.
point: Geophysical and bathymetric evidence rules out Late Cretaceous land causeways from Madagascar and India to Antarctica (Gunnerus Ridge, Kerguelen Plateau); Conrad Rise lay about 1,600 km from Antarctica
note: Refereed review-and-analysis paper, open access; abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Retraction: Geo-Archaeological prospecting of Gunung Padang buried prehistoric pyramid in West Java, Indonesia (Archaeological Prospection 31(2):199, doi:10.1002/arp.1932)
author: Archaeological Prospection editors (E. Ernenwein, G. Tsokas) and John Wiley & Sons
point: Retraction and its stated reason: dated soils not associated with anthropogenic features
note: Journal retraction notice after investigation with outside experts; full text read.

title: Archaean zircons in Miocene oceanic hotspot rocks establish ancient continental crust beneath Mauritius. Nature Communications 8: 14086. doi:10.1038/ncomms14086
author: Ashwal, L. D.; Wiedenbeck, M.; Torsvik, T. H.
point: Archaean zircons 2.5 to 3.0 Ga in a 5.7 Ma trachyte on Mauritius; crust of central-east Madagascar affinity, now about 700 km west; Mascarene Basin opened about 84 Ma; Seychelles is a partly emergent continental fragment of 40,000 to 45,000 square km with crust about 33 km thick
note: Refereed open-access primary study; full text read via Europe PMC.

title: So Fair a House: Gobekli Tepe and the Identification of Temples in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic of the Near East
author: Banning, E. B.
point: Scientific alternative: the buildings may be houses rich in symbolic content
note: Refereed Current Anthropology article with comments; abstract read via OpenAlex; later supported in part by domestic finds (Clare 2020).

title: Lost city 'could rewrite history' (BBC News Online, 19 January 2002)
author: Housden, Tom
point: How the Khambhat claim was reported: 36 m depth, city five by two miles, debris dated nearly 9,500 years, discovered by NIOT; response of Justin Morris (British Museum)
note: Journalism; framing and claim record only (gate 6).

title: The Planetary Grid: A New Synthesis (PDFy mirror on Internet Archive; c. 1984)
author: Becker, W., Hagens, B.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 2 caps at D; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Becker and Hagens proposed: grid anchored to the poles and the Great Pyramid; 121 great circles, 4,862 points
note: Mirror of the proponents' article; original venue (Pursuit?) not verified; cited only for its own words.

title: Evidence of humans in North America during the Last Glacial Maximum
author: Bennett, M. R., Bustos, D., Pigati, J. S., et al.
point: White Sands footprints bracketed by seed layers dated about 23 to 21 ka
note: Refereed Science paper; abstract read via OpenAlex; ages later tested by Pigati et al. 2023.

title: Apparent and true polar wander and the geometry of the geomagnetic field over the last 200 Myr
author: Besse, J. and Courtillot, V.
point: True polar wander is episodic, 30 to 50 km/Myr in fast tracks, about 30 degrees total in 200 Myr, no superfast episodes
note: Refereed JGR paper with its own APWP analysis; a 2003 correction exists (doi:10.1029/2003JB002684); abstract read via Crossref; refined in detail by later compilations.

title: Early seafloor spreading in the South Atlantic: new evidence for M-series magnetochrons north of the Rio Grande Fracture Zone (GJI 206(2):835-)
author: Bird, D. E., Hall, S. A.
point: Seafloor spreading in the South Atlantic by magnetochrons M4 to M0 (~131 to ~125 Ma)
note: Refereed geophysical study; abstract read.

title: The Secret Doctrine, vol. 2: Anthropogenesis
author: Blavatsky, H. P.
gates: gate 3 caps at D; gate 1 caps at B
point: What Blavatsky wrote about Lemuria as the 'third Continent' (vol. 2, p. 7)
note: Original text read in the 1888 first-edition scan. Advocacy for a religious-philosophical system built on the claim (coi 0, gate 3). Cited only for what Blavatsky wrote.

title: Researchers helpless as Bosnian pyramid bandwagon gathers pace (Science 314:1862, doi:10.1126/science.314.5807.1862a)
author: Bohannon, J.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 6 caps at C
point: Framing: EAA open letter (Dec 2006) calling the project a cruel hoax; Osmanagić's 2005 declaration and claimed 12,000-year-old civilisation
note: Science news story; quotes the EAA letter; framing and claim record only.

title: The graphic system and ancient records of the Mayas (Introduction to C. Thomas, A Study of the Manuscript Troano; Contributions to North American Ethnology vol. 5)
author: Brinton, Daniel G.
point: That Brasseur de Bourbourg found the Troano in Madrid in 1864, published a translation, and later said he had begun at the wrong end, read in the wrong direction and meant his readings as experiments
note: Contemporary scholarly account in a US government series, read as a Wikisource transcription (prov 1); historical point, so rec 2.

title: Simulating the ley hunter (Journal of the Royal Statistical Society A 143(2):109-126, doi:10.2307/2981985)
author: Broadbent, S. R.
point: Triad statistic for near-linear points; 52 Cornish megalithic sites' leys consistent with the sites' density distribution
note: Refereed statistics paper; abstract read.

title: Radiocarbon-based chronology for dynastic Egypt (Science 328:1554-1557, doi:10.1126/science.1189395)
author: Bronk Ramsey, C., Dee, M. W., Rowland, J. M., et al.
point: Reign of Djoser began 2691 to 2625 BCE (211 radiocarbon measurements, Bayesian model)
note: Refereed radiocarbon study; abstract read on PubMed.

title: University of Miami Radiocarbon Dates XIV
author: Calvert, P. M., Introne, D. S., Stipp, J. J.
point: Bimini Atlantis series UM-1359 to UM-1365: whole rock 2780-3500, shells 3510, cement 2750-2840 14C yr BP; cores from blocks at -4.6 m collected 1977 by E. Shinn
note: Refereed date list in Radiocarbon 21: 107-112; PDF read from Cambridge Core.

title: Circulating File: Atlantis, Vol. 1. A compilation of extracts from the Edgar Cayce readings (readings 958-3, 996-1, 440-5, 364-3)
author: Cayce, E. / Edgar Cayce Foundation
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 2 caps at D; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Cayce said: Poseidia to rise in 1968-69 (958-3, 28 June 1940); Bimini as remnant of Atlantis (996-1, 1926; 440-5, 1933)
note: Foundation compilation of the original reading transcripts; record of the claim only.

title: The Lost Continent of Mu: The Motherland of Man (William Edwin Rudge, New York)
author: Churchward, James
point: What Churchward claimed: a Pacific continent from north of Hawaii to Easter Island and Fiji, over 5,000 by 3,000 miles, sunk 12,000 years ago; based on 'Naacal tablets' and the Troano manuscript
note: Popular book with a thesis to sell and no checkable sources for its tablets; 1926 first edition scan (public domain mark); cited only for Churchward's words.

title: Gobekli Tepe, Turkey. A brief summary of research at a new World Heritage Site (2015-2019)
author: Clare, L.
point: Site dates about 9500 to 8000 calBC; PPNA about 9500-8700 and EPPNB about 8700-8200 calBC; domestic buildings, burial, rock-cut cistern; revision of the temple narrative; UNESCO inscription 2018
note: DAI e-Forschungsberichte report by the project's research coordinator on the excavation's own results; full PDF read; coi 1 as institutional report on its own site.

title: The Last Glacial Maximum
author: Clark, P. U., Dyke, A. S., Shakun, J. D., Carlson, A. E., Clark, J., Wohlfarth, B., Mitrovica, J. X., Hostetler, S. W., McCabe, A. M.
point: LGM timing: ice sheets at maximum 26.5 to 19-20 ka; NH deglaciation onset 19-20 ka
note: Refereed Science synthesis of 5704 14C, 10Be and 3He ages; abstract read via Europe PMC; widely used definition of the LGM.

title: Gobekli Tepe: Genesis of the Gods. The Temple of the Watchers and the Discovery of Eden (publisher's description)
author: Collins, A. / Bear & Company (Inner Traditions)
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 3 caps at D; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Collins claims: built in response to a global cataclysm by the Watchers of Enoch and the Anunnaki
note: Publisher's description (ISBN 9781591431428, May 2014); record of the claim only.

title: Europe's Lost Frontiers: exploring climate change, settlement and colonisation of the submerged landscapes of the North Sea basin using ancient DNA, seismic mapping and complex systems modelling (project 670518)
author: European Commission CORDIS
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 6 caps at C
point: Project existence, host (University of Bradford), dates (Dec 2015 to Nov 2021) and aims
note: EU project record; framing only.

title: The Lost City of Atlantis - Hidden in Plain Sight? Lost Ancient Human Civilizations (YouTube video, Bright Insight)
author: Corsetti, Jimmy
point: That Corsetti claimed in September 2018 that the Richat Structure is the most likely location of Atlantis; view count about 5.0 million when fetched
note: Self-published video funded through Patreon; upload date 2018-09-04 from page metadata; cited only for the claim's existence and wording (description text).

title: Palaeomagnetic evidence relevant to a change in the earth's radius. Nature 189: 45-47. doi:10.1038/189045a0
author: Cox, A.; Doell, R. R.
point: Record of the expansion proposals in circulation in 1961: Carey's 45 per cent increase in Earth's area since the Palaeozoic and Egyed's 0.4 to 0.8 mm per year radius increase; and that palaeomagnetism could test them
note: Refereed Nature paper by two USGS palaeomagnetists; abstract read on the USGS Publications Warehouse record. Recency 1: their test was later refined by McElhinny et al. (1978).

title: Physical features of Adam's Bridge interpreted from ICESat-2 based high-resolution digital bathymetric elevation model. Scientific Reports 14, 14896. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-65908-2
author: Dandabathula, G., Ghosh, K., Hari, R., Sharma, J., Sharma, A., Padiyar, N., Poonia, A., Bera, A. K., Srivastav, S. K. and Chauhan, P.
point: Adam's Bridge about 29 km, submarine continuation of Dhanushkodi and Talaimannar, about 1 km3, 99.98% submerged; Palk Strait 9 to 12 m average depth; Gulf of Mannar floor slopes to 36 m then drops; borings found 7 to 9 m sand over Holocene conglomerate/calcareous sandstone and coral
note: Refereed primary bathymetry by ISRO NRSC authors; boring results are reported from older surveys (cited within). Full text via Europe PMC (PMC11213924).

title: Human and cervid osseous materials used for barbed point manufacture in Mesolithic Doggerland
author: Dekker, J., Sinet-Mathiot, V., Spithoven, M., Smit, B., Wilcke, A., Welker, F., Verpoorte, A., Soressi, M.
point: Barbed points from Doggerland dated 9.5 to 7.3 ka 14C BP; two of ten made of human bone
note: Open-access refereed paper (J. Archaeol. Sci. Reports 35); abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Abrupt onset and termination of the African Humid Period: rapid climate responses to gradual insolation forcing. Quaternary Science Reviews 19, 347-361. doi:10.1016/S0277-3791(99)00081-5
author: deMenocal, P., Ortiz, J., Guilderson, T., Adkins, J., Sarnthein, M., Baker, L. and Yarusinsky, M.
point: African Humid Period 14.8 to 5.5 cal ka BP, when the Sahara was nearly completely vegetated with many perennial lakes (ODP Site 658C off Cap Blanc)
note: Refereed primary record, widely corroborated; timing of termination refined since (rec 1).

title: Ice-sheet collapse and sea-level rise at the Bolling warming 14,600 years ago
author: Deschamps, P., Durand, N., Bard, E., Hamelin, B., Camoin, G., Thomas, A. L., Henderson, G. M., Okuno, J., Yokoyama, Y.
point: MWP-1A timing 14,650 to 14,310 years ago; 12 to 22 m at Tahiti; >40 mm/yr
note: Refereed Nature paper on IODP Exp. 310 Tahiti corals; abstract read via Europe PMC; timing corroborated by Lambeck 2014 and Lin 2021.

title: The role of cult and feasting in the emergence of Neolithic communities. New evidence from Gobekli Tepe, south-eastern Turkey
author: Dietrich, O., Heun, M., Notroff, J., Schmidt, K., Zarnkow, M.
point: Layer III PPNA enclosures and Layer II PPNB buildings; central pillars about 5.5 m; at least 20 enclosures; no domesticated plants or animals; regional comparanda
note: Refereed Antiquity paper by the excavators; full PDF read; rec 1 as the sanctuary-only reading and the layer scheme were revised by Clare 2020.

title: Atlantis: The Antediluvian World (Harper & Brothers, New York; Gutenberg #4032; IA Atlantis1882)
author: Donnelly, Ignatius
point: What Donnelly claimed: an Atlantic continent opposite the Mediterranean, with ridge soundings as its backbone
note: Popular book with a thesis to sell; original text, cited only for Donnelly's words and argument. Page numbers from the 1882 contents list at https://archive.org/details/Atlantis1882.

title: Atlantis: The Antediluvian World (Part V, ch. VI, The African Colonies)
author: Donnelly, I.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Donnelly wrote about the dolmen-builders of Africa and Europe as colonists from Atlantis
note: Original text via Project Gutenberg; cited only for its own words and for the Faidherbe summary it reports.

title: Atlantis: The Antediluvian World (Part IV, ch. V, The Pyramid, the Cross, and the Garden of Eden)
author: Donnelly, I.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Donnelly wrote about pyramids on both sides of the Atlantic
note: Original text via Project Gutenberg; a politician's popular book; cited only for its own words.

title: Evolution of Ramasetu region as a link between India and Sri Lanka during the late Pleistocene and Holocene. Quaternary Research 111, 166-176. doi:10.1017/qua.2022.41
author: Dubey, K. M., Chaubey, A. K., Gaur, A. S. and Joglekar, M. V.
point: Buried channels across the Palk Strait; freshwater reservoir in the last glacial; seawater from about 8.5 ka; channels buried by about 7.0 ka; walkable link in dry MIS 2 seasons; not crossable without boats for about 7 ka
note: Refereed primary seismic study; single study not yet replicated (corr 1). Abstract via Crossref.

title: Foreword to Earth's Shifting Crust
author: Einstein, A.
point: What Einstein wrote in the foreword (pp. 1 to 2)
note: Original printed foreword; physicist writing outside geology; cited only as the record of his words.

title: History of Stonehenge
author: English Heritage
point: Stonehenge: henge ditch about 3000 BC; stone circle about 2500 BC
note: Heritage-body history page with footnotes; body manages the site.

title: Water dowsing: the Scheunen experiments (Naturwissenschaften 82:360-369, doi:10.1007/BF01134560)
author: Enright, J. T.
point: Peer-reviewed version of the Munich dowsing re-analysis (bibliographic record only)
note: Only the Springer record was reached; contested by Betz et al. 1996 in the same journal.

title: Testing dowsing: the failure of the Munich experiments (Skeptical Inquirer 23(1))
author: Enright, J. T.
point: Munich barn dowsing tests: ~500 candidates, 43 selected, 843 tests; results indistinguishable from chance
note: Author re-analysed the published data himself; magazine of a sceptics' organisation, so coi 1.

title: Eight glacial cycles from an Antarctic ice core
author: EPICA community members
point: Dome C ice core gives a climate record for the past 740,000 years
note: Refereed Nature paper; abstract read via Semantic Scholar; record later extended to 800 ka.

title: The Richat structure, Mauritania (Envisat MERIS image caption)
author: European Space Agency
point: Outer rim peak about 485 m above sea level; uplift and erosion origin
note: Agency web caption by communications staff; its 50 km diameter disagrees with the 40 km of the research papers, which the entry uses.

title: The Bering Strait was flooded 10,000 years before the Last Glacial Maximum
author: Farmer, J. R., Pico, T., Underwood, O. M., et al.
point: Bering Strait flooded from 46 ka until 35.7 (+3.3/-2.4) ka
note: Refereed PNAS paper (vol. 120); abstract read via OpenAlex and Crossref.

title: Evidence for an extraterrestrial impact 12,900 years ago that contributed to the megafaunal extinctions and the Younger Dryas cooling
author: Firestone, R. B., West, A., Kennett, J. P., et al.
point: What the impact hypothesis proposed in 2007 and on what evidence (not whether an impact occurred)
note: Refereed PNAS paper; abstract read via Crossref. As evidence that an impact happened it would score corr 0 and fall to D under gate 5; it is cited here only as the record of the proposal.

title: When the Sky Fell: In Search of Atlantis (outline, as quoted by Hancock)
author: Flem-Ath, R. and Flem-Ath, R.
point: What the Flem-Aths proposed, in their own words as reproduced by Hancock (Fingerprints of the Gods, ch. 50, p. 446)
note: The book itself (archive.org/details/whenskyfellinsea00flem) is lending-only and was not read; quotation is second-hand through Hancock.

title: The Continental Drift Controversy, vol. 2: Paleomagnetism and Confirmation of Drift (Cambridge University Press)
author: Frankel, H. R.
point: The palaeomagnetic case for drift built up in the 1950s: apparent polar wander paths showed the continents had moved relative to one another, broadly as Wegener proposed
note: University-press history based on archives and interviews. Only the publisher's description was read; cited for framing and the sequence of events, no numbers.

title: Leg 183 synthesis: Kerguelen Plateau-Broken Ridge, a large igneous province. Proc. ODP, Scientific Results 183. doi:10.2973/odp.proc.sr.183.015.2003
author: Frey, F. A.; Coffin, M. F.; Wallace, P. J.; Weis, D.
point: Kerguelen Plateau lavas erupted from about 119 Ma to about 34 Ma on igneous crust about 20 km thick; much of the plateau stood above sea level (wood, fern and pollen in overlying sediment); Proterozoic zircon in gneiss clasts at Site 1137 on Elan Bank shows continental crust fragments in the Indian Ocean
note: Refereed ODP synthesis of drilling results by the leg's co-chiefs; abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Santorini eruption radiocarbon dated to 1627-1600 B.C. Science 312, 548. doi:10.1126/science.1125087
author: Friedrich, W. L., Kromer, B., Friedrich, M., Heinemeier, J., Pfeiffer, T. and Talamo, S.
point: Olive tree buried by Minoan tephra wiggle-matched to 1627 to 1600 BCE (95.4%)
note: Refereed primary dating; calibration since revised (Pearson et al. 2018), so corr and rec 1. Abstract read via Europe PMC.

title: Questionable claims (Frontline 19(5), 2 to 15 March 2002)
author: Bavadam, Lyla
point: May 2001 announcement by Murli Manohar Joshi; finds dredged, no divers or photographs; archaeologists' objections (Agrawal, Menon, Raman, Ratnagar); two labs gave about 7,500 and 5,500 years for the wood
note: Magazine journalism quoting named archaeologists; read via Wayback Machine capture (prov 1); framing only.

title: Mapping Doggerland: The Mesolithic Landscapes of the Southern North Sea
author: Gaffney, V., Thomson, K., Fitch, S. (eds)
point: Seismic mapping of more than 23,000 km2 of the buried landscape; history of research (Reid 1913; Colinda find 1931; Godwin 1933)
note: Archaeopress monograph (ISBN 9781905739141) by the project team; sample PDF (front matter and chapter 1) read; rev 1 as editorial monograph; rec 1 as Lost Frontiers work has extended it.

title: Antarctic Ice Sheet variability across the Eocene-Oligocene boundary climate transition
author: Galeotti, S., DeConto, R., Naish, T., et al.
point: An ice sheet formed on Antarctica about 34 Ma; continental-scale ice reaching the coast by about 32.8 Ma
note: Refereed Science paper on a Ross Sea drill core; abstract read via OpenAlex; consistent with the long-established Eocene-Oligocene glaciation.

title: The breakup of East Gondwana: Assimilating constraints from Cretaceous ocean basins around India into a best-fit tectonic model. JGR Solid Earth 118. doi:10.1002/jgrb.50079
author: Gibbons, A. D., Whittaker, J. M. and Muller, R. D.
point: Ridge separating Greater India from Australia-Antarctica reached the southern tip of India about 126 Ma; India-Madagascar seafloor spreading about 94 to 84 Ma, unzipping from about 100 Ma
note: Refereed plate-kinematic model from magnetic and gravity data; one of several models, so corr 1. Abstract via Crossref.

title: A 3d model of Complex A, La Venta, Mexico (Digital Applications in Archaeology and Cultural Heritage 1:72-81, doi:10.1016/j.daach.2014.06.001)
author: Gillespie, S. D., Volk, M.
point: La Venta apogee ca. 800-400 BC (uncalibrated); earthen pyramid (Complex C) over 30 m high; clay architecture
note: Refereed paper; author PDF read in full.

title: Was the Black Sea catastrophically flooded in the early Holocene?
author: Giosan, L., Filip, F., Constatinescu, S.
point: Reconnection about 9400 years ago (about 8400 14C BP); pre-reconnection level about -30 m from the Danube delta; Bosphorus about 35 m, Dardanelles about 70 m deep; summary of Ryan's proposed >=50 m rise
note: Refereed QSR rapid communication (28: 1-6); accepted manuscript read from WHOI.

title: Magicians of the Gods (publisher's description)
author: Hancock, G. / Hachette UK (Coronet)
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 3 caps at D; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Magicians of the Gods claims: an advanced Ice Age civilisation destroyed 12,800 to 11,600 years ago; survivors settled at Gobekli Tepe and elsewhere
note: Publisher's marketing description; the book text itself was not reachable; record of the claim only.

title: The History of Creation, vol. 1 (English translation revised by E. Ray Lankester, 1876, of Natuerliche Schoepfungsgeschichte, 1868)
author: Haeckel, E.
point: What Haeckel wrote about Lemuria as the probable cradle of the human race (pp. 360-361)
note: Original text, read in the scan. A zoologist writing on geography and human origins (neighbouring field). Cited only for what Haeckel wrote.

title: Fingerprints of the Gods
author: Hancock, G.
point: What Hancock wrote about Antarctica, crust displacement and the ancient maps (Part I; ch. 50, p. 446; ch. 51, p. 451)
note: Popular book by a journalist with a thesis to sell; reposted scan of the Three Rivers Press edition; record of the claim only.

title: Lost city 'could rewrite history' (BBC News Online, 19 January 2002), quoting Graham Hancock
author: Housden, Tom (quoting Hancock, Graham)
point: Graham Hancock's words on the Khambhat finds
note: Second record: a proponent quoted in the press; Hancock sells books on lost civilisations (coi 0); cited only for his words.

title: Magicians of the Gods: The Forgotten Wisdom of Earth's Lost Civilization
author: Hancock, G.
point: What Hancock wrote about the Younger Dryas comet and the lost civilisation (ch. 4, ch. 5, ch. 9)
note: Popular book with endnotes, reposted ebook text without page numbers; record of the claim only.

title: Gobekli Tepe: Gradual evolution? Or transfer of technology? Or both?
author: Hancock, G.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 2 caps at D; gate 3 caps at D; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Hancock claims: Gobekli Tepe reflects technology transfer from a lost civilisation (quoting Ancient Apocalypse ep. 5, 2022)
note: Author's own website, 14 April 2024; read via Wayback capture; record of the claim only.

title: Rapid flooding of the Sunda Shelf: a late-glacial sea-level record
author: Hanebuth, T., Stattegger, K., Grootes, P. M.
point: Sunda Shelf sea-level record; MWP-1A up to 16 m within 300 years (14.6 to 14.3 ka)
note: Refereed Science paper; abstract read via Europe PMC; stage values also reproduced in Sathiamurthy & Voris 2006; rec 1 as later work (Hanebuth et al. 2009) refines the LGM termination.

title: Earth's Shifting Crust: A Key to Some Basic Problems of Earth Science
author: Hapgood, C. H. (with J. H. Campbell)
point: What Hapgood proposed in 1958: size, speed and date of the last crustal displacement (pp. 91, 249, 340)
note: Original text (Pantheon, 1958; Internet Archive scan); author a historian with no geological training arguing his own thesis; cited only for his own words.

title: Maps of the Ancient Sea Kings: Evidence of Advanced Civilization in the Ice Age
author: Hapgood, C. H.
point: What Hapgood claimed about the Piri Reis map, Queen Maud Land and the dates of the source maps (Preface; Antarctic maps chapter; Ohlmeyer letter)
note: Original text, 1996 Adventures Unlimited reprint of the 1966 book, reposted scan; record of the claim only.

title: The Path of the Pole
author: Hapgood, C. H.
point: What Hapgood proposed in 1970: Hudson Bay and Greenland Sea poles, shift 18 to 12 ka (Author's Note)
note: Original text (Chilton, 1970) read from a reposted copy on the Internet Archive (catalogued copy at archive.org/details/pathofpole0000hapg_1970 is lending-only); record of the claim only.

title: Sr-Nd-Pb composition of Mesozoic Pacific oceanic crust (Site 1149 and 801, ODP Leg 185). G-cubed 4(8). doi:10.1029/2002GC000421
author: Hauff, F.; Hoernle, K.; Schmidt, A.
point: The oldest in-place Pacific ocean crust, drilled in front of the Mariana and Izu-Bonin trenches, is 130 to 167 Ma
note: Refereed primary study; abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Kinematics of the South Atlantic rift (Solid Earth 4:215-253, doi:10.5194/se-4-215-2013)

author: Schoch, R. M.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 2 caps at C
point: Framing: Visočica and Pljesevica made of tilted Miocene sandstone, clay, mudstone, siltstone and conglomerate; blocks are naturally fractured beds
note: Boston University geologist who spent ten days at the site; personal site version; numbers taken from Sant et al. 2018 instead.

title: Gondwana land bridges. GSA Bulletin 43(4): 875-916. doi:10.1130/GSAB-43-875
author: Schuchert, C.
point: Schuchert's stated position among the schools of permanence and subsidence (opening paragraph)
note: Refereed GSA Bulletin paper by a leading palaeontologist. Only the publisher's opening-paragraph preview could be read, so data scored 1. Cited only for his position.

title: Radiocarbon dates and Bayesian modeling support maritime diffusion model for megaliths in Europe (PNAS 116(9):3460-3465, doi:10.1073/pnas.1813268116)
author: Schulz Paulsson, B.
point: Megalithic graves emerged in NW France 4794-3986 cal BC (most probably within 200-300 years); three phases of spread by sea; 2,410 dates
note: Refereed Bayesian synthesis of compiled radiocarbon dates; full text read on PMC.

title: The mammals of Madagascar. Quarterly Journal of Science 1 (April 1864): 213-219
author: Sclater, P. L.
point: What Sclater proposed and in what words (p. 219)
note: Original paper read in the Internet Archive scan of vol. 1; the record of the proposal. Cited only for what Sclater proposed, never for whether the continent existed.

title: The Lost Lemuria, with two maps showing distribution of land areas at different periods
author: Scott-Elliot, W.
gates: gate 3 caps at D; gate 1 caps at B
point: What Scott-Elliot wrote about the extent and age of Lemuria on his maps
note: Original Theosophical Publishing Society text read in the scan; the maps are said to derive from occult sources; direct stake in the claim. Cited only for what Scott-Elliot wrote.

title: Why a chain of limestone shoals between India and Sri Lanka has led to a political brawl (Scroll.in, 31 December 2022)
author: Deuskar, Nachiket
point: History of the dispute: Sethusamudram project, 2007 ASI affidavit and its withdrawal, 2017 Discovery programme, 2018 government position, 2022 statement in Parliament
note: Explanatory journalism with links to primary reports; framing only.

title: A global data set of present-day oceanic crustal age and seafloor spreading parameters. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 21, e2020GC009214. doi:10.1029/2020GC009214
author: Seton, M., Muller, R. D., Zahirovic, S. et al.
point: Early Jurassic ocean floor present in the Central and Equatorial Atlantic
note: Refereed global dataset built from magnetic anomaly identifications; consistent with independent reconstructions.

title: A global data set of present-day oceanic crustal age and seafloor spreading parameters. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 21, e2020GC009214. doi:10.1029/2020GC009214
author: Seton, M., Muller, R. D., Zahirovic, S. et al.
point: Pacific ocean crust reaches back to a Jurassic triangle in the western Pacific; mean age of ocean crust 64.2 Myr
note: Second record for a different point (Pacific floor ages, Mu entry).

title: Miocene and Pliocene ice and air from the Allan Hills blue ice area, East Antarctica
author: Shackleton, S., Hishamunda, V., Davidge, L., et al.
point: Allan Hills ice directly dated (40Ar deficit) to about 6 Ma; oldest continuous core 800 ka
note: Refereed PNAS paper, open access (PMC12595499); authors call the Miocene ages 'putative' and the ice stratigraphically complex, hence corr 1.

title: 50-Ma initiation of Hawaiian-Emperor bend records major change in Pacific plate motion. Science 313, 1281-1284. doi:10.1126/science.1128489
author: Sharp, W. D. and Clague, D. A.
point: Hawaiian-Emperor bend began near Kimmei Seamount about 50 Ma
note: Refereed primary 40Ar/39Ar dating; O'Connor et al. 2013 give 47.5 Ma for volcanism in the sharp bend, so the range is reported.

title: The expanding Earth at present: evidence from temporal gravity field and space-geodetic data. Annals of Geophysics 54(4). doi:10.4401/ag-4951
author: Shen, W.; Sun, R.; Chen, W.; Zhang, Z.; Li, J.; Han, J.
point: A contrary estimate: surface rising at 0.24 +/- 0.04 mm per year from ITRF2008 station heights, and 0.17 to 0.21 mm per year from gravity data
note: Refereed geodesy paper; abstract read via OpenAlex. Its result is not reproduced by Wu et al. (2011), so corroboration 1; reported as the other end of the range.

title: A Geologist's Adventures with Bimini Beachrock and Atlantis True Believers
author: Shinn, E. A.
point: Coring of the Bimini stones; oriented cores show consistent bedding dip toward deep water; beachrock identical to modern beach; 14C ages 2000 to 4000 years (McKusick & Shinn 1980); history of the Cayce link; Gifford & Ball 1980
note: Skeptical Inquirer 28(1) article by the USGS geologist who did the work, citing his refereed papers; full PDF read.

title: When was the Sun Pyramid built? Maintaining the status quo at Teotihuacan, Mexico (Latin American Antiquity 26(2):221-241, doi:10.7183/1045-6635.26.2.221)
author: Sload, R.
point: Sun Pyramid construction began in the first century A.D.; later dates reflect ritual and modification
note: Refereed Bayesian re-analysis; abstract read; the other end of the range.

title: Review of W. L. Friedrich, Fire in the Sea: The Santorini Volcano: Natural History and the Legend of Atlantis. Geological Magazine 137(5), 593
author: Sparks, R. S. J.
point: A volcanologist's judgement that there is 'at least a plausible case' linking Santorini with the Atlantis legend
note: Expert book review with editorial review only and no data; framing only.

title: Timing of hot spot-related volcanism and the breakup of Madagascar and India. Science 267: 852-855. doi:10.1126/science.267.5199.852
author: Storey, M.; Mahoney, J. J.; Saunders, A. D.; Duncan, R. A.; Kelley, S. P.; Coffin, M. F.
point: Madagascar and India broke apart about 88 Ma: 17 argon-argon ages from the 1,500 km rifted east margin of Madagascar average 87.6 +/- 0.6 Ma
note: Refereed primary geochronology; the date is used in every later reconstruction (e.g. Ali and Hedges 2024 give 85 Mya). Abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: The Face of the Earth (Das Antlitz der Erde), vol. 1 (English translation by Hertha B. C. Sollas, 1904; German vol. 1 first published 1885)
author: Suess, E.
point: What Suess wrote when naming Gondwana-Land (p. 596), and his view that the Indian Ocean formed by subsidence within it
note: Original text by the leading geologist of the day, read in the Internet Archive scan; a monograph without formal refereeing, so gate 1 caps at B. Cited only for what Suess proposed.

title: Inside the Sun Pyramid at Teotihuacan, Mexico: 2008-2011 excavations and preliminary results (Latin American Antiquity 24(4):403-432, doi:10.7183/1045-6635.24.4.403)
author: Sugiyama, N., Sugiyama, S., Sarabia G., A.
point: Sun Pyramid dated A.D. 170-310 and tunnel A.D. 140-240; three construction stages
note: Refereed excavation report; abstract read; disputed by Sload 2015.

title: Rejection of Holliday et al.'s alleged refutation of the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis
author: Sweatman, M. B., Powell, J. L. and West, A.
point: That proponents contest the 2023 refutation and cite replications
note: Refereed reply in Earth-Science Reviews by proponents of the hypothesis (West is a 2007 co-author, so coi 1); abstract read via OpenAlex; cited only for the existence and content of the reply.

title: Beringian Standstill and Spread of Native American Founders
author: Tamm, E., Kivisild, T., Reidla, M., et al.
point: Original statement of the Beringian standstill from mtDNA
note: Open-access refereed paper; abstract read; hypothesis corroborated by later ancient-DNA and Y-chromosome work.

title: A Study of the Manuscript Troano (Contributions to North American Ethnology vol. 5), Preface
author: Thomas, Cyrus
point: That the Troano was read in 1882 as chiefly a ritual or religious calendar
note: Original study of the manuscript in a US government series; superseded in detail by modern decipherment (rec 1); Wikisource transcription (prov 1).

title: Phanerozoic polar wander, palaeogeography and dynamics
author: Torsvik, T. H., Van der Voo, R., Preeden, U., et al.
point: The South Pole has remained close to East Antarctica since about 230 Ma (p. 334)
note: Same paper, third point; agrees with all standard plate reconstructions.

title: Phanerozoic polar wander, palaeogeography and dynamics
author: Torsvik, T. H., Van der Voo, R., Preeden, U., et al.
point: Lithospheric net rotation averaging about 0.12 deg/Myr over 150 Myr, peak 0.33 deg/Myr at 60 to 50 Ma (p. 356 to 357)
note: Same paper, second point; net-rotation estimates depend on the reference frame and vary between models, hence corr 1.

title: Phanerozoic polar wander, palaeogeography and dynamics
author: Torsvik, T. H., Van der Voo, R., Preeden, U., et al.
point: Four Mesozoic TPW episodes 250 to 100 Ma at 0.45 to 0.8 deg/Myr; cumulative TPW near zero since the Late Carboniferous; 626 poles
note: Refereed review with new compilation and analysis (Earth-Science Reviews 114, 325 to 368); full text read from the authors' posted PDF (earthdynamics.org).

title: A Precambrian microcontinent in the Indian Ocean. Nature Geoscience 6: 223-227. doi:10.1038/ngeo1736
author: Torsvik, T. H.; Amundsen, H.; Hartz, E. H.; Corfu, F.; Kusznir, N.; Gaina, C.; Doubrovine, P. V.; Steinberger, B.; Ashwal, L. D.; Jamtveit, B.
point: Zircons 660 to 840 Ma and more than 1,971 Ma in Mauritian beach-sand lavas; gravity inversion shows thick crust from Mauritius to the Seychelles; Mauritia separated from Madagascar and was broken into a ribbon by ridge jumps as the Mascarene Basin opened between 83.5 and 61 Ma
note: Refereed primary study; abstract read on nature.com. Corroborated by Ashwal et al. 2017 with zircons taken directly from Mauritian rock.

title: Alfred Wegener (1880-1930), UCMP History of Science pages
author: University of California Museum of Paleontology
point: How Wegener's theory was received (Chamberlin's criticism, Du Toit and Argand as supporters) and that plate tectonics was accepted by almost all geologists by the late 1960s
note: Museum education page, author unnamed, no references. Tier C: framing only; no number in the entries rests on it.

title: Turkey: The Piri Reis World Map (1513) in the Topkapı Palace Museum Library. Nomination form, International Memory of the World Register, ID 2016-34
author: General Directorate of Cultural Heritage and Museums, Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Turkey
point: Map found in the Topkapı Palace Library in 1929; Revan Köşkü no. 1633; parchment 87 cm long; surviving part about one third; among the earliest maps showing Terra Australis
note: Heritage-body nomination prepared by the institution that holds the map (institutional interest); editorial review by UNESCO.

title: Megaliths of Carnac and of the shores of Morbihan (World Heritage List 1725)
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
point: Carnac megaliths built during the Neolithic, c. 5000-2300 BCE
note: Heritage-body description, inscribed 2025.

title: Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa Dolmen Sites (World Heritage List 977)
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
point: Korean dolmens are funerary monuments; dolmens worldwide mostly 2nd and 1st millennia BCE; >440 and >500 dolmens at Gochang and Hwasun
note: Heritage-body statement of Outstanding Universal Value.

title: Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe (World Heritage List 1336)
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
point: Kush a power 8th c. BCE-4th c. CE; Meroe site of most royal burials from 3rd c. BCE; pyramid tombs
note: Heritage-body statement of Outstanding Universal Value.

title: Gebel Barkal and the Sites of the Napatan Region (World Heritage List 1073)
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
point: Napatan 900-270 BC and Meroitic 270 BC-350 AD cultures; pyramids of Kurru and Nuri, steep angles, 9th c. BC-4th c. AD funerary tradition
note: Heritage-body statement of Outstanding Universal Value.

title: Gobekli Tepe (World Heritage List entry 1572)
author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
point: Coordinates N37 13 23.671 E38 55 20.51; inscription 2018
note: Heritage-body listing; read via Wayback capture (live page returned 403).

title: Understanding plate motions, This Dynamic Earth
author: Kious, W. J., Tilling, R. I. (USGS)
point: Spreading rates from under 2.5 cm/yr (Arctic Ridge) to over 15 cm/yr (East Pacific Rise)
note: USGS general-interest publication.

title: This Dynamic Earth: Developing the theory
author: Kious, W. J.; Tilling, R. I. (USGS)
point: Hess and Dietz: seafloor spreading from ridges and consumption at trenches, which explains why the Earth does not get bigger; symmetric magnetic stripes and young rocks at ridge crests; drift revived by ocean-floor data from the 1950s; Mid-ocean ridge >50,000 km long; young rocks at the crest getting older away from it; magnetic stripes; new crust at the ridge
note: USGS explainer; standard profile.

title: This Dynamic Earth: Historical perspective
author: Kious, W. J.; Tilling, R. I. (USGS)
point: Wegener's two articles of 1912; Glossopteris fossils in now-polar regions; Jeffreys's objection that continents could not plough through the ocean floor; Pangaea began to break up about 225 to 200 Ma
note: USGS explainer; standard profile.

title: This Dynamic Earth: Hotspots
author: U.S. Geological Survey (Kious, W. J. and Tilling, R. I.)
point: Oldest rocks on Kauai about 5.5 Ma; oldest exposed rocks on the Big Island under 0.7 Ma; chain made by the Pacific plate over a hotspot
note: Survey explainer; the page notes later debate on hotspot fixity, which does not affect the age progression cited.

title: This Dynamic Earth: Inside the Earth
author: Kious, W. J.; Tilling, R. I. (USGS)
point: Oceanic crust is about 5 km thick; continental crust averages about 30 km; Oceanic crust about 5 km thick; continental crust averages about 30 km
note: USGS General Interest Publication with agency review; standard explainer profile.

title: This Dynamic Earth: Understanding plate motions
author: Kious, W. J.; Tilling, R. I. (USGS)
point: Spreading on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge averages about 2.5 cm per year (25 km per million years); Mid-Atlantic Ridge spreading about 2.5 cm/yr; Atlantic grew over 100 to 200 Myr; Iceland straddles the ridge; Krafla rifting 1975 to 1984, about 7 m
note: USGS explainer; standard profile.

title: 10,000 years on the Bering Land Bridge: Ancestors of Native Americans paused en route from Asia (press release on Hoffecker, Elias & O'Rourke 2014, Science 343: 979-980)
author: University of Utah (via ScienceDaily)
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 6 caps at C
point: Framing: Hoffecker et al. argued people lived on the land bridge about 25,000 to 15,000 years ago amid shrub tundra
note: University press release; framing only; the Science perspective itself could not be read.

title: The Madrid Codex: New Approaches to Understanding an Ancient Maya Manuscript, ch. 1 'Research methodologies and new approaches to interpreting the Madrid Codex' (University Press of Colorado)
author: Vail, Gabrielle and Aveni, Anthony (eds)
point: Madrid Codex holds about 250 almanacs organised on the 260-day ritual calendar (rain ceremonies, agriculture, hunting, year-end rites, eclipses); extant Maya codices Late Postclassic, c. 1250 to 1520
note: Refereed scholarly monograph; read from the publisher's excerpt PDF.

title: Magnetic anomalies over oceanic ridges. Nature 199: 947-949 (7 September 1963). doi:10.1038/199947a0
author: Vine, F. J.; Matthews, D. H.
point: Publication record: Vine and Matthews's 1963 paper on magnetic anomalies over ocean ridges
note: Refereed Nature paper; only the bibliographic record was reachable (data 1). Content described through USGS This Dynamic Earth.

title: Maps of Pleistocene sea levels in Southeast Asia: shorelines, river systems and time durations
author: Voris, H. K.
point: Shoreline maps at 10 to 120 m contours; sea level at or below -40 m for more than half of the last 250 kyr
note: Refereed J. Biogeography paper (27: 1153-1167); abstract read via OpenAlex; rec 1 as later maps (Sathiamurthy & Voris 2006) refine it.

title: Formal definition and dating of the GSSP for the base of the Holocene using the Greenland NGRIP ice core, and selected auxiliary records
author: Walker, M., Johnsen, S., Rasmussen, S. O., et al.
point: Base of the Holocene (end of the Younger Dryas / GS-1) at 11,700 yr b2k, maximum counting error 99 yr, ratified by IUGS
note: Refereed paper defining the ratified GSSP (J. Quaternary Sci. 24, 3 to 17; online 2008); abstract read via Crossref.

title: A great wave: the Storegga tsunami and the end of Doggerland?
author: Walker, J., Gaffney, V., Fitch, S., Muru, M., Fraser, A., Bates, M., Bates, R.
point: Storegga tsunami c. 8150 BP; Dogger Island by 9000 cal BP; 1 to 4 m global rise 8400 to 8200 cal BP; last islands gone c. 7000 cal BP; tsunami not the final flooding
note: Open-access refereed Antiquity paper from the Europe's Lost Frontiers team with new core and sedaDNA data; read at Cambridge Core.

title: Early British Trackways, Moats, Mounds, Camps, and Sites
author: Watkins, A.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Watkins proposed in 1922 (sighting lines called leys)
note: Original text via Project Gutenberg; antiquarian lecture printed in Hereford; cited only for his own words.

title: The Old Straight Track: its Mounds, Beacons, Moats, Sites and Mark Stones (Methuen; first published 29 Oct 1925; 4th ed. scan)
author: Watkins, A.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 5 caps at D
point: What Watkins asked in the 1925 preface
note: Internet Archive scan (Wellcome Library copy) of the 1948 fourth edition; preface dated August 1925.

title: Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane, 2nd ed., ch. 1 (Project Gutenberg transcription)
author: Wegener, A.
point: What Wegener proposed (continents once joined, split and drifted apart) and his own account that the first two publications appeared in 1912 and the first edition in 1915 (p. 10 to 12 and note 30)
note: Original record of what Wegener argued and when; recency 2 for the historical point. Gate 1 caps at B.

title: Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane, 2nd ed., ch. 1 'Landbruecken, Permanenz der Ozeane und Isostasie' (Project Gutenberg transcription)
author: Wegener, A.
point: Wegener's summary of the land-bridge consensus (including the 'lemurische' bridge said to break in the Lower Eocene) and his argument that isostasy forbids bridges sinking to the deep-sea floor (pp. 7 to 9)
note: Original text of the 2nd edition (Vieweg, 1920), faithfully transcribed by Project Gutenberg. Recency 2 because cited as the record of his argument; the isostasy argument has held up. Monograph without formal refereeing, gate 1 caps at B.

title: Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane, 2nd ed., ch. 1 (Project Gutenberg transcription)
author: Wegener, A.
point: Wegener's statement that Lemuria can be reconstructed by smoothing the folds of High Asia, which brings India against Madagascar (p. 10)
note: Original text; cited as the record of how Wegener recast Lemuria. Gate 1 caps at B.

title: EPICA Dronning Maud Land EDML ice core drilling protocol
author: Wilhelms, F. et al.
point: EDML drill site at 75.0025 S, 0.0684 E; recovered core 2,774 m long
note: Data record in the PANGAEA repository; editorial data curation rather than peer review, so gate 1 caps it at B.

title: Ley Lines in Question (World's Work, 232 pp., ISBN 0-437-19205-9)
author: Williamson, T., Bellamy, L.
point: That a book-length examination of ley claims by a landscape historian exists (1983); content not read
note: Only the UEA catalogue record was reached; not cited for any finding.

title: Isthmian links. GSA Bulletin 43(4): 917-952. doi:10.1130/GSAB-43-917
author: Willis, B.
point: Willis's framework: granitic continents, basaltic ocean floors in isostatic equilibrium, permanence, and narrow isthmian links modelled on Panama
note: Refereed GSA Bulletin paper by a leading structural geologist. Only the publisher's section summary could be read (data 1). Cited only for what Willis proposed.

title: The mystery of Bosnia's ancient pyramids (Smithsonian, December 2009)
author: Woodard, C.
gates: gate 1 caps at B; gate 6 caps at C
point: Framing: University of Tuzla cores showed alternating conglomerate, clay and sandstone; 'flatirons' comparison by P. Heinrich (LSU)
note: Magazine feature; framing only.

title: Accuracy of the International Terrestrial Reference Frame origin and Earth expansion. GRL 38: L13304. doi:10.1029/2011GL047450
author: Wu, X.; Collilieux, X.; Altamimi, Z.; Vermeersen, B. L. A.; Gross, R. S.; Fukumori, I.
point: Combining SLR, VLBI, GPS and DORIS data, the Earth's mean radius is not changing to within a 1-sigma uncertainty of 0.2 mm per year
note: Refereed primary geodesy by JPL, IGN and TU Delft authors; abstract read via OpenAlex.

title: Late Quaternary history of the Black Sea: an overview with respect to the Flood Hypotheses
author: Yanko-Hombach, V., Gilbert, A. S., Dolukhanov, P.
point: The gradual/oscillating position: lake -140 to -50 m 16-13 ka, about -20 m by 11 ka, about -50 m in the YD, gradual rise to about -20 m after reconnection at about 9.5 ka; no archaeological signal of a flood; 1997 and 2003 hypothesis dates (7.2 and 8.4 ky BP)
note: EGU General Assembly abstract (Geophys. Res. Abstr. 8, 00359) by specialists summarising their volume; cited for their reconstruction and position.

title: The Black Sea Flood Question: Changes in Coastline, Climate, and Human Settlement
author: Yanko-Hombach, V., Gilbert, A. S., Panin, N., Dolukhanov, P. M. (eds)
point: Existence and editors of the 2007 volume
note: Springer/NATO Science Series volume; bibliographic record only (Crossref), content not read.

title: Geology of the Yonaguni Jima district (Quadrangle series, scale 1:50,000)
author: Yazaki, K.
point: Yonaguni built of the Middle Miocene Yaeyama Group; Aragabana Formation sandstone-shale alternation >300 m on the SE coast; faulted horst-graben pattern; dips 10-30 deg E on the east side
note: Geological Survey of Japan map explanatory text; English abstract read; rec 1 because Miocene stage assignment may have been refined since 1982.

title: Ancient single origin for Malagasy primates. PNAS 93: 5122-5126. doi:10.1073/pnas.93.10.5122
author: Yoder, A. D.; Cartmill, M.; Ruvolo, M.; Smith, K.; Vilgalys, R.
point: All living Malagasy lemurs descend from one ancestor; lemurs and the Afro-Asian lorises (Strepsirrhini) share an African ancestor
note: Refereed primary molecular study, open access. Recency 1: later work refines the dates but keeps the single origin.

title: Divergence dates for Malagasy lemurs estimated from multiple gene loci: geological and evolutionary context. Molecular Ecology 13: 757-773. doi:10.1046/j.1365-294x.2004.02106.x
author: Yoder, A. D.; Yang, Z.
point: Molecular age of the lemur clade: about 62 to 65 Ma in nearly all analyses
note: Refereed Bayesian dating study; abstract read via OpenAlex. Later studies (e.g. Herrera and Davalos 2016) give somewhat different dates, so corroboration 1 and recency 1.

title: Situs Gunung Padang: Kebudayaan, Manusia, dan Lingkungan (Semiotika, Bandung; 2nd printing 2019 with Disparbud Jabar; ISBN 978-602-6885-09-8)
author: Yondri, L.
point: Charcoal beneath terrace walls: 1986±110 BP (Terrace I, ~117 BC), 2014±30 BP (Terrace II, ~47 BC), 1845±100 BP (Terrace IV, ~45 BC as reported)
note: Excavator's monograph from his 2016 Padjadjaran doctoral dissertation; read via an Internet Archive copy; co-published by the provincial tourism office.
